title: PJM 2028/2029 Capacity Auction Cleared at $325/MW-Day Cap, 6.8 GW Short; Uncapped Price Would Have Been $555/MW-Day
content: The 2028/2029 PJM capacity auction results posted July 14, 2026 cleared at the cap of $325/MW-day. The auction came up 6.8 GW short of its reliability requirement. Without the collar, the uncapped price would have been $555/MW-day, or $777/MW-day in the ComEd zone. The collar mechanism is extended for two more auctions at current levels ($175-$325/MW-day) per the FERC order on April 21, 2026. The 2029/2030 auction results post December 22, 2026, and remains the final scheduled auction with the collar in place. The reliability backstop procurement (RBP) was designed to fill exactly this shortfall. FERC issued an order September 29 partially accepting PJM's RBP proposal but found three areas potentially unjust: cost allocation, Transmission Owner Exit rules, and LSE collateral requirements.
explanation: PJM ran its yearly auction that pays power plants to be available in 2028 and 2029. A capacity auction is the market that buys that standby power, priced in dollars per megawatt-day (MW-day), which is the cost of keeping one megawatt ready for one day. The price hit the allowed ceiling of $325 per MW-day, and the region still came up 6.8 gigawatts short of the reliability target. Without the collar (a regulator-set floor and cap), the price would have printed $555, or $777 in the Chicago-area ComEd zone. The collar stays in place through the 2029/2030 auction. A backup purchase program (RBP) is meant to fill the shortfall, but FERC only partly approved it. This can mean higher capacity charges on power bills in PJM states, and it is a signal that standby supply is tight. This is not investment advice.
